question: Should Crabbox adopt this v3 signed-user-token design that carries an encrypted GitHub OAuth credential, revalidates membership with a five-minute positive cache, fails closed after cache expiry, and forces existing v2 token holders to log in again?
rationale: This changes the coordinator authentication boundary, outage behavior, and upgrade semantics; code review can check implementation shape but cannot choose the supported security policy for maintainers.

options.title: Accept after fixes and proof
options.body: Approve this design once the branch is rebased, the hard-coded live test and changelog edit are fixed, and redacted live output demonstrates the membership path.

options.title: Require server-side revocation state
options.body: Pause this PR and ask for a design that avoids carrying the GitHub OAuth credential inside client-held user tokens.

options.title: Defer for policy design
options.body: Keep the linked security issue open while maintainers decide outage grace, cache TTL, and migration guarantees before implementation.

recommendation.title: Accept after fixes and proof
recommendation.body: Approve this design once the branch is rebased, the hard-coded live test and changelog edit are fixed, and redacted live output demonstrates the membership path.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle owns the recent auth/token history and authored the current PR branch, making it the best available routing owner for the design choice.
